202611171427-n2-never-name-a-number-firs.topic: 'Never name a number first' is only half right: the salary-expectations script for the recruiter's first call

script.title: "Never Name a Number First" Is Only Half Right

beats.narration: "Never name a number first" is only half right.
"I'm flexible" sounds unprepared, and the recruiter still has a number in mind. It's theirs.
Try: "Based on what I'm seeing for this role, I'm targeting eighty to ninety thousand. How does that fit your range?"
Make the bottom of that range a number you'd genuinely accept. That's the one they'll hear.
If the role is vague, the old rule holds. Ask: "What's the budgeted range?" Some US states require posted ranges, so check the listing first.
You have less leverage here. A researched range still beats a shrug.
Save this script for the next time you need it, and tell me in the comments which piece of career advice I should test next.

script.description: The old rule says never name a number first, but dodging the salary question on a recruiter's first call can backfire. Here is the exact wording I'd try, plus when staying quiet still makes sense. Norms vary by country and industry, so check your local context.
